title: Simulation of Half Adder and Full Adder Circuit in Multisim
aim: To construct and verify the truth tables of Half Adder and Full Adder combinational arithmetic circuits.
apparatus_components: OR Gate IC 7432 (for Full Adder Carry-Out combination)
Interactive Digital Inputs (A, B, Cin) and Output Probes (Sum, Cout)
theory: A Half Adder adds two 1-bit binary numbers A and B, producing Sum = A ⊕ B and Carry = A · B. Because it cannot accept a carry-in from a lower significant stage, a Full Adder adds three 1-bit binary numbers (A, B, Cin) and produces Sum = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin and Cout = AB + (A ⊕ B)Cin = AB + BCin + ACin.
equations: Full Adder SUM = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin
Full Adder CARRY (Cout) = A·B + Cin·(A ⊕ B) = A·B + B·Cin + A·Cin
circuit_topology: Half Adder: 1 XOR + 1 AND in parallel across (A, B). Full Adder: two cascaded Half Adders with their carry outputs combined by an OR gate.
simulation_type: Digital Combinational Truth-Table Verification (4 states for Half Adder, 8 states for Full Adder)
procedure:
1. For Half Adder, wire inputs A, B to an XOR gate (Sum) and an AND gate (Carry).
2. Verify all 4 input states (00, 01, 10, 11).
3. For Full Adder, cascade a second XOR and AND gate with input Cin, and OR the two carry terms.
4. Verify all 8 input states (000 through 111).
expected_observations: Full Adder outputs Sum=1 when an odd number of inputs are 1 (001, 010, 100, 111) and Cout=1 when at least two inputs are 1 (011, 101, 110, 111).
result: The Half Adder and Full Adder circuits were simulated and their truth tables were verified.
common_mistakes: Using an XOR gate instead of an OR gate to combine the two intermediate carry outputs in a Full Adder
Forgetting the Carry-In (Cin) input when building the Full Adder truth table

viva_concepts.q: What is the main limitation of a Half Adder?
viva_concepts.a: A Half Adder has no Carry-In (Cin) input, so it cannot add the carry bit propagated from a previous lower-order bit position.

viva_concepts.q: Why is the Full Adder Carry-Out expression `AB + BCin + ACin` called the majority function?
viva_concepts.a: Because Cout is 1 whenever a majority (2 or all 3) of the inputs A, B, Cin are 1.

viva_concepts.q: How do you build a Full Adder from two Half Adders?
viva_concepts.a: Connect the first Half Adder to A and B to get S1 = A⊕B and C1 = AB. Connect the second Half Adder to S1 and Cin to get Sum = S1⊕Cin and C2 = S1·Cin. Combine C1 and C2 with an OR gate to get Cout.

viva_concepts.q: How many 2-input XOR, AND, and OR gates are in a standard Full Adder?
viva_concepts.a: Two 2-input XOR gates, two 2-input AND gates, and one 2-input OR gate (5 gates total).

viva_concepts.q: For which input row of the Full Adder are both Sum and Cout equal to 1?
viva_concepts.a: Only when A = 1, B = 1, and Cin = 1 (binary 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = 11_2).

viva_concepts.q: Can the final OR gate in a two-half-adder Full Adder be replaced by an XOR gate?
viva_concepts.a: Yes, because C1 = A·B and C2 = (A⊕B)·Cin can never both be 1 simultaneously, so C1 + C2 is identical to C1 ⊕ C2.

viva_concepts.q: How many Full Adders are needed to build a 4-bit ripple carry adder?
viva_concepts.a: One Half Adder (for the LSB) and three Full Adders, or four Full Adders with the first Cin tied to 0.

viva_concepts.q: If A = 1, B = 0, Cin = 1, what are S1, C1, C2, Sum, and Cout?
If a student's Full Adder gives Cout = 0 when A=1, B=1, Cin=1, what mistake did they likely make?
viva_concepts.a: They likely connected the second AND gate to (A, Cin) incorrectly or omitted the OR gate combining C1 and C2.

viva_concepts.q: Which minterms produce Sum = 1 and which produce Cout = 1 in a Full Adder?

EXPERIMENT-8

Date:

SIMULATION OF HALF ADDER AND FULL ADDER CIRCUIT IN MULTISIM
Aim:
To design and simulate the half adder and full adder circuits using Multisim and verify their
truth tables.
Apparatus Required:
•

Computer with Multisim software installed

•

Basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, XOR)

•

Digital input switches (Logic Toggles)

•

Digital output indicators (LEDs)

Circuit diagram

Procedure:
Part 1: Half Adder
1. Open Multisim:
o

Launch Multisim on your computer.

2. Create a New Project:
o

Go to File > New > Project.

o

Name your project and click Create.

3. Place Components for Half Adder:
o

Select the Place menu and choose Component.

o

In the Select a component window, choose TTL as the family.

o

Select the following components and place them on the schematic workspace:
▪

25 | P a g e

XOR gate (7408)

▪

AND gate (7432)

▪

Digital input switches (Logic Toggles)

▪

Digital output indicators (LEDs)

4. Connect the Circuit:
o

Connect the inputs of the XOR gate to the input switches. This gate will
produce the SUM output.

o

Connect the inputs of the AND gate to the same input switches. This gate will
produce the CARRY output.

o

Connect the outputs of the XOR gate and the AND gate to separate LEDs to
display the SUM and CARRY respectively.

5. Configure Inputs and Simulate:
o

Set the input switches to all possible combinations (00, 01, 10, 11).

o

Run the simulation and observe the outputs for each combination.

6. Verify the Truth Table:
o

The expected truth table for the half adder is:
Input A Input B Sum (XOR) Carry (AND)

2. Place Components for Full Adder:
o

Select the Place menu and choose Component.

o

In the Select a component window, choose TTL as the family.

o

Select the following components and place them on the schematic workspace:
▪

XOR gates (7408)

▪

AND gates (7432)

▪

OR gate (7432)

▪

Digital input switches (Logic Toggles)

▪

Digital output indicators (LEDs)

3. Connect the Circuit:
o

27 | P a g e

For the SUM output:
▪

Connect two input switches (A and B) to the inputs of the first XOR
gate.

▪

Connect the output of this XOR gate and the third input switch (Cin) to
the inputs of the second XOR gate. The output of this second XOR
gate will be the SUM.

o

o

For the CARRY output:
▪

Connect inputs A and B to the inputs of the first AND gate.

▪

Connect the output of the first XOR gate and Cin to the inputs of the
second AND gate.

▪

Connect the outputs of the two AND gates to the inputs of the OR gate.
The output of this OR gate will be the CARRY.

Connect the outputs of the second XOR gate (SUM) and the OR gate
(CARRY) to separate LEDs.

4. Configure Inputs and Simulate:
o

Set the input switches to all possible combinations (000, 001, 010, 011, 100,
101, 110, 111).

o

Run the simulation and observe the outputs for each combination.

5. Verify the Truth Table:
o

The expected truth table for the full adder is:

code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Topology Classification: EXACT MANUAL TOPOLOGY (Half Adder and Full Adder Digital Circuit (Experiment 8))
# 1. Run Digital Logic Truth Table Verification
print('=== DIGITAL TRUTH TABLE VERIFICATION ===')
rows = []
for idx in range(8):
    A, B, C = (idx >> 2) & 1, (idx >> 1) & 1, idx & 1
    sum_bit = A ^ B ^ C
    carry_bit = (A & B) | (B & C) | (A & C)
    sop_y = 1 if idx in (1, 3, 6) else 0
    rows.append((A, B, C, sum_bit, carry_bit, sop_y))
    print(f'A={A} B={B} C={C} | Sum={sum_bit} Carry={carry_bit} | SOP_Y={sop_y}')

# 2. Extract digital signals & 3. Plot digital timing waveforms
t = np.arange(8)
arr = np.array(rows)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(10, 7), sharex=True)
labels = ['Input A', 'Input B', 'Input C', 'Output Y']
cols = [0, 1, 2, 3 if 'ADDER' in 'HALF_FULL_ADDER' else 5]
for ax, col_idx, lbl in zip(axes, cols, labels):
    ax.step(t, arr[:, col_idx], where='post', linewidth=2)
    ax.set_ylabel(lbl)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.2, 1.2)
    ax.grid(True)
axes[0].set_title('Digital Logic Truth-Table Timing Waveforms')
axes[-1].set_xlabel('Input State Index (0..7)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('digital_truth_table_waveforms.png', dpi=150)
plt.show()
